compounding_issues: All 5 sessions failed at the model layer: claude-sonnet-5 hit its subscription session limit, so every session produced 0 tokens, 0 tool calls, 0 files (exit code 1). No session ever built on a prior one.

Seed codebase mismatch: the tier2_small TypeScript seed is a single-file Express/JWT/SQLite auth API (index.ts, with a bad_seed hardcoded_secret variant), which is entirely unrelated to the static site generator CLI the story asks for — the agent would have had to discard the entire seed.

Because no code was produced, session 5 (incremental builds/caching) has nothing to build on; the greenfield→feature→integration→refactor→cross_cutting arc exists only in commit labels, not in artifacts.

Empty placeholder commits: each session commit adds only a 3-line .instrument/session_N.jsonl transcript, so the git history is vacuous and the analysis pipeline recorded 0 lines added/removed across all 5 commits.
key_decisions: Story seed selection: reusing the shared tier2_small Express auth API as the starting codebase for a static_site_gen story, which forces a full codebase replacement rather than incremental evolution.
bad_seed condition application: using the pre-degraded variant (hardcoded_secret) rather than a clean seed, compounding the seed mismatch.

The session design itself (greenfield → template engine → dev server → plugin system → incremental builds) is a sound progression and remains the one defensible architectural choice — it just was never executed.
No runtime architectural decisions were made by the agent because it never ran: the resulting architecture is the seed's single-file Express API, untouched.
story_review.trajectory_description: The quality arc is flat at zero: the run is operationally void. Sessions 1-5 each hit the Claude session limit before the first assistant turn, so there is no code, no tests, no diffs, and no measurable improvement or degradation between commits — the entire 'story' consists of five placeholder transcripts appended to an unrelated seed. The nominal session ordering would have been coherent, but no artifact exists to evaluate, so any assessment of quality across sessions is vacuous.
story_review.summary: This is a failed run, not a story: claude-sonnet-5 hit its session limit in all 5 sessions, so the commit sequence contains zero implementation and the seed (an unrelated Express auth API) was never modified.
